ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · عمرو بن جبير: Amr b. Jubayr limits witnessing to repayment by a guardian of money borrowed from an orphan while poor and repaid after becoming solvent. {"id": "4:6/q37", "question": "Why call witnesses when property is delivered?", "turns_on": "Whether witnessing chiefly protects the guardian, records repayment, or confirms receipt.", "positions": [{"id": "4:6/q37/p1", "position": "Witnesses establish receipt and prevent disputes or suspicion", "reasons": "IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · القاضي أبو يعلى: Witnesses at delivery are a precaution, not an obligation; evidence protects the orphan from falsely denying receipt and the guardian from an oath if delivery is disputed. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author: The preceding warning against consuming wealth hastily before the orphan grows up shows why suspicion of guardians is well-founded and strengthens the case for witnessing delivery. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author: Witnessing protects the orphan from injustice and short delivery because the guardian cannot convincingly claim to have transferred the assets without witnesses; al-Rāzī says both the command’s wording and its purpose require it. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author: Witnessing the handover is commanded to secure the assets and clear suspicion; scholars differ whether it is recommended, since a guardian is trusted, or obligatory, since he cannot testify in his own favor against heirs. BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author: Witness the transfer to prove receipt and prevent suspicion, dispute, and liability; the chosen position and Malik require proof from the guardian, unlike Abu Hanifa. NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author: When returning the property, obtain witnesses to prove receipt and avoid denial or a disputed oath. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author: Witnessing delivery prevents disputes and suspicion, protects the guardian from liability if the ward denies receipt, reassures the ward, and marks release from restraint for ordinary dealings. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author: After the orphan reaches puberty and discernment, the guardian must hand over the estate and have the recipient's receipt witnessed to prevent later denial. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author: Guardians must document the return of an orphan’s property because maturity and sound judgment vary, and witnesses prevent disputes and protect both sides. BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author: Witnesses should attest that the heirs received the estate, protecting the guardian from suspicion and dispute and clearing responsibility. BURSEVI, d. 1127 · مالك والشافعي: Malik and al-Shafiʿi require proof and do not accept a guardian’s claim of delivery without witnesses. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author: Witnessing the handover establishes receipt and discharges the guardian, reducing suspicion and disputes and better preserving trust; the author's school treats it as recommended. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author: Witnessing delivery makes the amount clear, permits later recovery of assets found to have remained with the guardian, protects the guardian from later claims, and prevents disputes. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author: Witnessing may be recommended to protect the guardian's own right, or obligatory to prevent disputes and serve public order, like documenting debts in 2:282. | mentions 2:282 IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · مالك: Malik does not accept a guardian's unsupported claim that he delivered the property; Ibn al-Faras says otherwise the command to document would be pointless because denial exposes the guardian to liability.
